related_questions.question: Why is my period 2 weeks late but not pregnant?

text_blocks.snippet: A period that is two weeks late, when a pregnancy test is negative, can be due to various factors beyond pregnancy. Stress, changes in weight, intense exercise, hormonal imbalances, or certain medical conditions can all affect menstrual cycles.
snippet_highlighted_words: Stress, changes in weight, intense exercise, hormonal imbalances, or certain medical conditions can all affect menstrual cycles

text_blocks.snippet: Potential reasons for a late period when not pregnant:

list.snippet: Stress: High stress levels can disrupt hormone production, impacting ovulation and causing missed or late periods.
Hormonal Imbalances: Conditions like Polycystic Ovary Syndrome (PCOS) or thyroid issues can lead to irregular periods.
Weight Fluctuations: Being significantly underweight or overweight can affect hormone levels and menstrual cycles.
Intense Exercise: Excessive exercise can sometimes lead to missed periods, particularly in athletes.
Medications: Certain medications, including some types of birth control, can cause irregular bleeding patterns.
Illness: Acute or chronic illnesses can also impact the menstrual cycle.
Perimenopause: This transitional phase before menopause can cause irregular periods.

list.title: 1. Retest for pregnancy:
list.snippet: If it's been a week or two since the first negative test, consider retesting to be absolutely sure.

list.title: 2. Track your cycle:
list.snippet: Note the start date of your periods, and any other symptoms you may be experiencing.

list.title: 3. Consult a doctor:
list.snippet: If your period is consistently late or if you have other concerning symptoms, it's best to consult a healthcare professional for proper evaluation and guidance.

list.title: 4. Lifestyle changes:
list.snippet: If stress is a factor, try incorporating stress-reducing techniques like exercise, meditation, or spending time in nature.

list.title: 5. Consider other factors:
list.snippet: If you've recently started a new medication, experienced significant weight changes, or have been under increased stress, these could be contributing factors.
